rationale: The workflow already implements the dependency-cache optimization (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE): it restores/saves the Haskell cabal store via actions/cache@v4 keyed by runner.os, matrix.ghc, and hashFiles('cabal.project.freeze'), with restore-keys, keeping installation and all tests. The measured GHA-CACHE evidence concerns adding a cache where none existed; here one is already present with lockfile-plus-environment inputs, so adding another cache step would be an unrelated/duplicate change. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (fail-fast: true) is contraindicated because the job deliberately uses fail-fast: false across multiple GHC versions and operating systems to preserve full build/test coverage and diagnostics; canceling remaining matrix cells would reduce required coverage. No other pattern's preconditions are met: there is no representative per-job duration history for a safe custom timeout, schedule suppression could miss Hackage/dependency rebuilds, and change-aware filtering could skip config/dependency-affected builds. Therefore no supported workflow_yaml change preserves the intended coverage.
